title: Production attempt entries are stamped `at: ""` — the sweep passes now_iso="" and nothing substitutes a real timestamp
evidence: sweep.gleam:164 `Ok(run(db_conn, deps, "", sentry, default_batch_limit))`; sweep.gleam:705 `#("at", json.string(at))`; sweep_handler.gleam:39 `now_iso: ""`; run/5 doc: "`now_iso` is an ISO-8601 timestamp string, or "" to let Postgres default to now() (production passes ""; tests pin the clock)" — but $1 is consumed only by the SELECT WHERE (`COALESCE(NULLIF($1, '')::timestamptz, now())`); the JSONB append `attempts = attempts || $2::jsonb` never falls back to now(). messages.gleam: "[{at, channel, outcome, detail}]; the sweep stamps `at` when it builds the guarded append".
detail: Every sweep-appended attempt entry (T0/co-nudge/reminder1/reminder2) carries `at:""` in production — the log loses its timestamps and the §8.3 warm-handoff email renders blank times (`render_attempt_line` prints `entry.at`). Spec AD-4 attempt shape is `{at, channel, outcome, detail}`.
recommended_fix: Stamp `at` from the DB: pass `''` and have each append SQL use `jsonb_set`/to_jsonb(now()) for missing `at`, or call wisp.now()/clock in Gleam before building entries; add a test asserting non-empty `at`.

title: Warm-handoff email renders a fabricated `reminder_2` entry from the stale pre-advance log instead of the real appended entries
evidence: sweep.gleam:530 `parse_attempts_entries(row.attempts)` then `|> list.append([AttemptEntry(at: now_iso, channel: "email", outcome: "reminder_2", detail: "T+96h reminder")])` — `row.attempts` is the pre-advance SELECT value; the committed append for this tick holds the 2 real ChannelOutcome entries (email+sms, vocabulary Delivered/Skipped/Failed per messages.gleam). messages.gleam:394/408 "We've tried to reach them " <> count <> " times over the last 4 days. The attempt log:"
detail: AC5 requires the notification to render the attempt log. The email undercounts the row's real log by one, shows an entry that doesn't exist in the row (`reminder_2` is not an Outcome), and omits the actual email/sms outcomes. Comment claims "the advance already committed it to the row" — the row was never re-read.
recommended_fix: Re-read the row's attempts after the advance (or return the appended entries from the guarded UPDATE) and render the actual log; drop the synthetic mirror entry.

title: Manual-fire handler threads the live `config.sentry`, contradicting spec item 7's pinned `sentry_client.Disabled` ("manual runs don't escalate")
evidence: Spec item 7: "Handler threads `sentry_client.Disabled` (manual runs don't escalate). Wired in `router.gleam`." sweep_handler.gleam: `sentry: config.sentry` in both SendDeps and `sweep.run(... sentry: config.sentry ...)`, and the module doc: "Runs against the live config (DB + Resend + Twilio + Sentry), so failures escalate to Sentry the same as a scheduled tick."
detail: Implementation is the opposite of the spec's pinned decision: an ops manual fire now Sentry-captures every per-row failure (ReferenceSweepRowFailed), producing alert noise for deliberate runs. The handler's own comment asserts the reversed intent.
recommended_fix: Thread `sentry_client.Disabled` into `sweep.run` (and deps.sentry) in `handle_run_reference_checks`, matching spec item 7; update the module doc comment.

title: Story Verify items "fake-clock server tests per cadence step" and "guarded-update race test" are not delivered; no test ever pins `now_iso`
evidence: Test helper: `sweep.run(db, no_key_deps(), now_iso: "", sentry: sentry_client.Disabled, batch_limit: 100)` — every test passes ""; steps are fast-forwarded via `rearm_due` (`UPDATE reference_call SET next_attempt_at = now() - interval '1 hour'`), and no test executes two ticks concurrently. The required no-duplicate-T0-across-retry test (line 257) is real and asserts `second.invited == 0`.
detail: The pinned-clock path (`$1` param + the `at` stamp) is entirely untested — precisely how the `at:""` defect slipped through. The sequential retry test covers AC3's retry case; a true concurrent-writer race test is absent.
recommended_fix: Add a fake-clock test passing a pinned `now_iso` per cadence step and asserting the `at` stamp, plus a concurrent double-tick test asserting one advance wins.

title: Due-SELECT failure returns an empty summary and exits 0 — the job logs "sweep complete: due=0" and Cloud Run marks the tick successful
evidence: `case sql.sweep_due_reference_calls(db, now_iso, batch_limit) { Error(err) -> { capture(sentry, "", "due-select failed: " <> query_error(err), "select") empty_summary(0) } ... }` and main() logs `"reference_checks sweep complete: " <> ... "due=" <> ...` on every Ok, then halts 0 (entrypoint: `case catch reference_checks@sweep:main() of nil -> erlang:halt(0)`).
detail: AD-15's per-tick completion log claims success (due=0) when the tick couldn't run at all, and the job is not marked failed, so job-failure alerting never fires. Sentry capture does fire, so the failure isn't fully silent — a liveness-reporting gap.
recommended_fix: Distinguish select-failure from empty-run in RunSummary (e.g. a `select_failed` flag), log an error line, and exit non-zero (erlang:halt(1)) on tick-level failure.
